label: first copy step (recall_idx 1) after echoing first token, esp. v followed by 2/o/g/h
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.03% of steps). About 90% of activation mass is on one step: the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), where the input is the echoed first original token and the model outputs orig(1). Among those steps it fires on only ~0.3%, chosen by a token conjunction. The echoed first token is strongly enriched for v (48% of mass), with weaker contributions from i, s, p, l, u, b. The upcoming outputs orig(1)/orig(2) are enriched for 2, o, g, h, i, 3. Top activations are v followed by 2/o/g within short sequences (L=3-4 are over-represented). Being at recall_idx 1 alone gives F1 ~0.01. The conjunction v and next_out in {2,o,h,g} gives F1 ~0.23 (precision 0.20, recall 0.27), and adding more conditions did not help much. It is almost silent at t<3, at the delimiter, and at copy steps after recall_idx 2. Small leftover activity appears late in the original phase (t=3-6) and right after z/0 inputs. Magnitude is highest when the first token is v and the next tokens are from {2,o,g}. I did not find a clean rule that covers the token selectivity.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+5.44), orig_idx=3 (+4.11), prev_tok=z (+4.04), t=4 (+3.73), in_tok=i (+3.70), orig2=o (+3.59). Lower it: in_tok=2 (-2.37), n_digits=0 (-1.78), n_digits=1 (-0.99).
